Zara (ml-onboard): Heads up — I just brought up an HF SentencePiece model (spm-chat-small) and the smoke tests show weird sentinel tokens leaking into chat outputs. Looks like <mask> is being emitted as <s> in some contexts.
Sam (tokenizers): ugh. Do you have an example output?
Zara (ml-onboard): short repro: prompt 'Replace the word with <mask> in the sentence.' -> model returns 'Hello <s> world' instead of replacing with mask content. Also noticed kv-cache misalignment when continuing the same convo.
Mike (runtime): kv-cache misalignment + wrong token ids screams index drift during conversion. Did you use our convert_spm_to_bpe script or the HF tokenizer CLI?
Zara (ml-onboard): used our convert_spm_to_bpe wrapper (recent commit). Command was:
```bash
python tools/convert_spm_to_bpe.py \
  --spm model/tokenizer.model \
  --out tokenizer.json --vocab-out vocab.txt --merges-out merges.txt
```
Sam (tokenizers): two things to check: 1) special_tokens ordering in tokenizer.json, 2) vocab <-> ids ordering after writing vocab.txt. SentencePiece preserves internal ids; if we regenerate vocab file sorted lexicographically we can reorder the indices.
Anya (eval): this explains a drop we saw in QA evals yesterday: F1 down ~2.6 pts on masked-fill tests. Might be same cause.
Mike (runtime): I pulled the conversion output. In our run the vocab.txt was written with enumerate(sorted(vocab)) which sorts surface tokens. That will flip indices compared to spm ids. If config.json points to mask_token_id downstream we get wrong symbol bound to mask id.
Sam (tokenizers): exact. SentencePiece uses id order that includes unused placeholders sometimes. BPE expects vocab index = id. Our conversion must preserve original id permutation.
Zara (ml-onboard): confirmed: running this snippet shows mismatch:
```py
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
for s in ['<mask>', '<s>', '<pad>', '<unk>']:
    print(s, t.token_to_id(s))
```
Outputs show mask=3 but model's spm reported mask id=220.
Mike (runtime): That would make the runtime read token id 3 embedding (BOS) when model expects 220, so output becomes BOS-like token text. KV cache lookups will index by position expecting 220 and get wrong entries -> misaligned continuations.
Anya (eval): did this surface after quantization? We also tested a q4_0 build which seemed noisier.
Zara (ml-onboard): it happened pre-quant. Quantization amplified the symptom but wasn't root cause.
Sam (tokenizers): fix: preserve id mapping when exporting. In convert_spm_to_bpe.py change from writing sorted(vocab.items()) to iterating by original id. Pseudopatch:
```py
# bad
for tok in sorted(vocab):
    write(tok)
# good
for id in range(spm_model.vocab_size()):
    tok = spm_model.id_to_piece(id)
    write(tok)
```
Mike (runtime): short-term runtime hotfix: we can map tokenizer ids to model ids at adapter load-time. Something like:
```py
# adapter remap
remap = {tok_id_from_tokenizer[tk]: spm_id_from_manifest[tk] for tk in special_tokens}
adapter.apply_special_token_remap(remap)
```
but long-term we should keep converter correct.
Zara (ml-onboard): agreed. I pushed a branch with the id-preserve change and added an assert that roundtrip(token, id) holds for first 1k ids.
CI-bot: CI: convert_spm_to_bpe tests failed on main (token id roundtrip assertion), new branch created: fix/spm-id-preserve-1932
Sam (tokenizers): also watch out for Unicode normalization differences. We saw earlier that NFKC normalization before piece extraction changes pieces slightly and causes subtle mismatches. Ensure we don't normalize differently between spm export and tokenizer.json write.
Anya (eval): added a unit in eval-harness that tokenizes a canonical prompt with both hf-spm and converted tokenizer and diffs token ids+strings. Will gate bring-up on that.
Mike (runtime): once conversion fix lands, I'll add a runtime guard: if majority of special tokens map to different ids, fail early with a clear error (and print mapping). Avoids silent regressions.
Zara (ml-onboard): thanks — deploying conversion fix now. For current production pinned model, I applied runtime remap hotfix and re-ran critical evals — mask-fill MRR recovered to baseline.
Sam (tokenizers): nice. Can we add a short blurb in docs about "preserve spm id order when converting" and the rationale (kv-cache + special token binding)?
Zara (ml-onboard): yes, I'll open a tiny docs PR.
Mike (runtime): lesson: token id equality is an operational contract between tokenizer and weights. Any converter that reorders vocab breaks that contract in subtle ways (not just pretty tokens).
Anya (eval): adding regression test to daily canary — if eval drops on masked tasks, it will block promoting that model.
Zara (ml-onboard): closing loop: branch merged, hotfix in prod, docs PR drafted. Thanks all :thumbsup: :eyes:
